subject: DPA deletion matrix & snapshot purge timeline (logs, prompts, backups)

Subject: DPA scope — deletion timelines for logs / backups / prompts

Hi Evelyn / Karthik,

Thanks for the initial DPA we received. Our DPO has a couple of targeted follow-ups before we can sign: we need a clear deletion "matrix" that lists the retention and deletion behavior for: application logs (access/error/trace), backups & snapshots (daily/weekly fulls), prompt data (user prompts & assistant responses), and any KV-cache or ephemeral traces used by the runtime.

Specifically:
- Exact retention windows (SLA) for each artifact type.
- Whether deletion from primary stores also removes data from backups/snapshots, and the expected purge timeline for backups.
- Any differences for accounts with HIPAA PHI.
- Controls for legal hold / export for audits (how are these handled vs. deletion).

Can you provide a single spreadsheet or matrix and a short engineer-friendly summary? We need enough detail to feed our privacy team and our procurement/legal folks.

Attached is a short form our security team uses (acme-datarequest-form.pdf) — feel free to populate and return. If faster, a 30-min call early next week works.

Best,
Jamie

DPO, Acme Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DPA scope — deletion timelines for logs / backups / prompts

Jamie — thanks for the clear list. I attached a draft deletion matrix (dpa-deletion-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a diagram that summarizes our backup lifecycle. High level here so your team can triage quickly: 

- Application logs (access, error, trace): default retention 90 days in primary log store. Prompts are not stored in plain-text inside logs.
- Prompt & response retention: ephemeral by default — 30 days for hosted API by default, configurable down to 0. No persistence beyond the configured window unless customer opts in for troubleshooting/eval storage.
- KV & runtime caches: ephemeral in-memory by design; persisted caches (for model acceleration) are TTLed and purged within 7 days after the last access.
- Backups & snapshots: daily snapshots retained 90 days; weekly full snapshots retained 365 days. Backups are immutable at snapshot time; we perform logical deletions that mark data for purge and then garbage-collect across snapshot copies. Estimated full purge from backups for a specific customer object is up to 120 days from request, depending on snapshot schedule.
- HIPAA customers: we offer a reduced retention default and an option for accelerated backup purge (SLA windows can be contracted).
- Legal hold: we support export/escrow and can freeze deletion for documented legal obligations; such holds must be requested via support with required paperwork.

Action items: Karthik — can you confirm the K/V cache TTL language and provide a short note on practical purge verification steps (logs to show purge completed)? Marissa — can you add the legal-hold intake link and the contact for accelerated purge SLA in the matrix?

I can do a 30-min call Monday if that helps.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Enterprise Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA scope — deletion timelines for logs / backups / prompts

Evelyn / Marissa — quick technical confirmation and a couple of clarifications to include in the matrix: 

- Logs: retention default 90d; can be reduced per-customer to 30d or 7d via account config. For deletion requests we run a two-phase process: (1) delete from active index/store within 24–72 hours; (2) redact or mark records in older shards and kick off shard GC. We keep an audit record of deletion events.

- Backups/snapshots: snapshots are incremental; data referenced by older incremental blobs may remain until the blob is eligible for GC. For an object-level deletion we perform reachability analysis to identify all blobs that reference the object and schedule them for GC; practical purge completion varies with snapshot cadence. Typical customer-observable completion: 30–120 days depending on when snapshots run. For HIPAA-graded customers we can negotiate a 45-day maximum purge SLA as an add-on.

- Prompts: hosted API prompts are written to an encrypted store when retention >0 is selected. Default 30d. For customers with "no retention" option we only keep prompts in transit and in ephemeral cache; nothing is written to persistent stores. 

- KV cache & accelerator state: in-memory first; persisted checkpoints (for performance) are TTLed and removed within 7 days after last use. We can run a verification job: after purge request we will produce a report listing purge jobs executed and hashes of deleted keys.

- Evidence: I recommend we provide: (a) a populated deletion matrix (attached), (b) a sample purge audit report (redactable), and (c) a short diagram explaining snapshot GC flow (attached: logs-retention-diagram.png).

I can run a test purge on our staging tenant for Acme if you want a demonstration — requires a scheduled maintenance window of ~2 hours.

-Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

Jamie — attaching the requested materials: dpa-deletion-matrix-v1.xlsx (filled with the fields above), logs-retention-diagram.png, and the short form you sent back populated. Summary of our commitments below for your privacy and procurement teams: 

- Default retention: logs 90d, prompts 30d (configurable).
- Backup purge: object-level deletion from backups expected to complete within 30–120 days depending on snapshot schedule; HIPAA add-on supports a contracted 45-day maximum.
- KV/cache: purged within 7 days after last access; verification hashes available on request.
- Legal hold: preserves data until released; will suspend scheduled GC.

Next steps: 1) Please confirm whether Acme wants the HIPAA accelerated purge SLA and whether you require shorter log retention defaults. 2) If you want a demonstration, we can schedule a 2-hr maintenance window to run a staged purge and provide a purge audit report. 3) I'll loop in our Contracts team if you want the 45-day SLA as a DPA addendum.
